question: The clean twin carries 3 Metadata trees (6 Metadata nodes) on three kinds of host: WorldInfo, Transform, PhysicalMaterial. How many arrive?

rows.note: The yardstick. Every checker on this page reads this file.

Only hosts that become glTF nodes can carry a packet. The WorldInfo and material trees are lost, and rules S1 and S2 fail out loud. The CIDOC-CRM class reference arrives typed (S4 1 of 1). Khronos validator: 0 errors.

rows.tool: fault-lab x3d_usd 0.1 (this demo's own; not a general exporter), usd-core 0.26.11
rows.note: Every prim, including a Material and a Scope, takes customData, so all three hosts keep their tree. 30 pxr validators: 0 errors. This converter is the demo's own, built to measure the ceiling.

Fixed in the add-on. The Transform's tree rides on the object that stands for it, the material's on the Blender material, the WorldInfo's on the scene. Any other host is kept on the scene, never dropped.
Every tree returns value for value on the same kind of host (compared by x3dsem). The file is valid against the X3D 4.0 XSD with 0 semantic errors (x3d_mcp 8205047).
The trees now travel as plain extras on the node, the material and the scene. They are not KHR_xmp_json_ld packets, so a JSON-LD tool will not find them without knowing the X3D shape.

rows.tool: Blender USD exporter, custom properties on
rows.note: Still nothing. Blender's USD exporter writes simple custom properties only and skips nested ones. Closing this needs the trees flattened to strings or a USD export hook.
